LESSON: MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Musical Instruments

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Musical Instruments. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. improvise body percussions to accompany songs for creativity and imagination and for enjoyment,
2. improvise percussion instruments using locally available materials for creativity and imagination,
3. improvise percussion accompaniment to songs and share them with others. dances for enjoyment. rhythmic pattern on improvised percussion instruments as the rest sing familiar songs, or for sound effects in a story.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. improvise body percussions to accompany songs for creativity and imagination and for enjoyment,
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to improvise body percussions to accompany songs for creativity and imagination and for enjoyment,. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. improvise percussion instruments using locally available materials for creativity and imagination,
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to improvise percussion instruments using locally available materials for creativity and imagination,. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. improvise percussion accompaniment to songs and share them with others. dances for enjoyment. rhythmic pattern on improvised percussion instruments as the rest sing familiar songs, or for sound effects in a story.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to improvise percussion accompaniment to songs and share them with others. dances for enjoyment. rhythmic pattern on improvised percussion instruments as the rest sing familiar songs, or for sound effects in a story. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At home, obey your parent when they ask you to wash your plate. That shows obedience.

Example 2: Tell the truth if you break a cup. Saying what really happened is honesty.

Example 3: Thank God for your family before you sleep. A short prayer can be: “Thank you God for today.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Musical Instruments.
2. Explain Musical Instruments to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Musical Instruments.
4. Show that you can: improvise body percussions to accompany songs for creativity and imagination and for enjoyment,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Musical Instruments. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Musical Instruments important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. improvise body percussions to accompany songs for creativity and imagination and for enjoyment,
2. improvise percussion instruments using locally available materials for creativity and imagination,
3. improvise percussion accompaniment to songs and share them with others. dances for enjoyment. rhythmic pattern on improvised percussion instruments as the rest sing familiar songs, or for sound effects in a story.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
